Answer: C
Reason: The admission chest X-ray (Figure 1) shows bilateral alveolar opacities consistent with pulmonary edema, which has significantly cleared by the discharge film (Figure 2). In the context of near-drowning or salt water aspiration, this rapid resolution is characteristic of non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema responding to supportive care (such as oxygen therapy and positive pressure ventilation), rather than diuretics or antibiotics.
